chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn al-Rabīʿ, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
If the menstruating woman becomes pure before al-ʿAṣr, she performs al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr. But if she becomes pure at the end of the time of al-ʿAṣr, she performs al-ʿAṣr.

So this does not conflict with the first report, because his statement, 'if she becomes pure before the time of al-ʿAṣr,' may mean that this was during the time of al-Ẓuhr. For that reason, making up al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr became obligatory upon her. But if it were the time of al-ʿAṣr only and nothing else, then nothing would be obligatory upon her except the salat of al-ʿAṣr.

key_terms.قَضَاءُ: making up or performing what has become due
key_terms.وَقْتِ: the legally designated time of the salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: If a menstruating woman becomes pure before al-ʿAṣr, must she pray al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr or only al-ʿAṣr?
ai.summary: This report gives a legal ruling regarding a menstruating woman who attains ritual purity before the end of the prayer times. If she becomes pure early enough before al-ʿAṣr, she must perform both al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr, while if she becomes pure only at the very end of al-ʿAṣr time, only al-ʿAṣr is due.
